items.section: When to get tested / Type 1 diabetes
items.short_quote: Having ketones in your urine indicates you have type 1 diabetes instead of type 2.
items.comparison_quote: People with type 2 diabetes can also develop DKA.
items.issue: Source-scope conflict on using urine ketones to infer diabetes type. Preserve both sources. Do not infer that positive urine ketones exclude type2.
items.suggestion: Quarantine type-inference excerpt from clinical-rule ingestion; professional reviewer must resolve interpretation and appropriate evidence. Do not delay emergency response to determine diabetes type.

items.section: Types of tests / Glucose tolerance test / At 2 hours
items.issue: The same page places140 mg/dL in both normal and prediabetes ranges. This is a directly observed internal boundary inconsistency; the correct clinical boundary has not been newly adjudicated here.
items.suggestion: Quarantine overlapping range from rule ingestion and seek professional correction with applicable diagnostic guideline; preserve original source wording.

items.section: Conditions that can increase risk / Elevated blood pressure
items.short_quote: between 120/80 mm Hg and 129/80 mm Hg
items.comparison_quote: Systolic is 120-129 mm Hg and Diastolic is less than 80 mm Hg.
items.issue: Elevated-category shorthand with diastolic80 differs from the explicit diastolic<80 condition in CDC's other page. Definitions are US-specific and pages display different dates.
items.suggestion: Preserve regional/version context and quarantine classification wording until professionally adjudicated; do not apply US definition as a China guideline.
